# Tokenized Gold: DBS Bank to Offer Retail Access Starting in 2026

Singapore’s largest bank, DBS, has announced it will provide retail clients access to **tokenized gold**, a move set to democratize ownership of the precious metal. The offering, scheduled for the second half of 2026, allows customers to buy DBS Physical Gold Tokens directly through the bank's popular digibank platform. This initiative follows a series of successful digital asset pilots, including the tokenization of structured notes on Ethereum and support for Franklin Templeton's money market fund token.

The introduction of a bank-grade tokenized commodity addresses a significant gap in the market. [According to the announcement](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/06/11/singapore-bank-dbs-to-offer-tokenized-gold-to-retail-customers), each token corresponds to one gram of physical gold, securely stored in a DBS vault in Singapore. This structure provides direct, fractional ownership of a real-world asset (RWA) with the security and trust of a major financial institution.

## DBS Paves the Way for Retail Gold Tokenization

The decision by DBS to bring a tokenized version of a traditional safe-haven asset to the retail market signals a major shift in digital finance. For years, direct access to physical gold has been predominantly reserved for institutional and high-net-worth investors. While retail customers could invest in gold-backed funds or ETFs, they did not have direct, divisible ownership of the underlying metal. This new product changes that dynamic entirely.

The bank’s plan to manage the entire token lifecycle, from issuance to custody, ensures a closed-loop, secure environment. By avoiding third-party protocols or custodians, DBS minimizes counterparty risk and simplifies the user experience. Investors will be able to trade and hold the tokens within the familiar interface of their existing banking application.

### What is Tokenized Gold?

Tokenized gold represents physical gold recorded on a blockchain. Each digital token is a claim on a specific quantity of real gold held in a secure, audited vault. This digital wrapper allows the gold to be divided into smaller fractions, traded 24/7, and transferred almost instantly. It combines the intrinsic value of physical gold with the efficiency and transparency of blockchain technology.

## A Closer Look at Bank-Grade RWA Infrastructure

The integrity of any tokenized asset hinges on the quality of its underlying infrastructure. DBS is leveraging its status as a regulated financial institution to offer what it calls 'bank-grade' tokenization. This approach is designed to build confidence among both retail and institutional investors who may be wary of decentralized alternatives. The bank is also exploring a potential listing on the DBS Digital Exchange (DDEx), which would expand access to accredited investors.

### The Significance of In-House Custody

By managing custody internally, DBS provides a level of assurance that is often missing in the broader digital asset space. Each token is directly backed by physical bullion held in the bank’s own Singapore-based vault. This vertical integration means customers have a direct claim on gold held by a trusted, regulated entity, removing layers of complexity and potential points of failure. The bank has noted that demand for physical gold from its wealth clients has more than doubled in the last three years, highlighting the timeliness of this retail-focused product.

### Building on Previous Digital Asset Success

This venture is not DBS's first entry into the world of tokenization. The bank has been an active participant in Singapore's Project Guardian, an initiative exploring institutional DeFi. In 2025, DBS successfully tokenized structured notes on the Ethereum network and listed sgBENJI, the token for Franklin Templeton’s money market fund. This experience with different forms of RWAs has provided a strong foundation for launching a more ambitious retail product.

## Context and Future Outlook for Tokenized Assets

The move by DBS is part of a much larger trend toward the tokenization of real-world assets. From real estate and private equity to commodities and fine art, financial institutions are exploring ways to make traditionally illiquid assets more accessible and efficient. The market for RWAs is projected to expand into a multi-trillion dollar industry by 2030.

### The Broader Trend of RWA Tokenization

Financial analysts see RWA tokenization as a critical bridge between traditional finance (TradFi) and the emerging digital asset economy. By placing real assets on a blockchain, issuers can unlock new liquidity, automate complex processes like dividend payments, and reach a global investor base. DBS’s initiative with gold serves as a powerful blueprint for other banks, demonstrating how to merge the security of traditional finance with the innovation of blockchain. As regulatory frameworks mature, we can expect to see an acceleration of similar products from major financial players worldwide.

## Conclusion

DBS Bank's plan to offer **tokenized gold** to retail customers is a landmark development in the adoption of real-world assets. By providing a secure, regulated, and accessible way to invest in physical gold, the bank is setting a new standard for how traditional assets can be integrated into the digital economy. For traders and investors, this move opens up a new, highly liquid avenue for portfolio diversification, backed by the trust of a global financial leader.

## FAQs

**1. What is a DBS Physical Gold Token?**

A DBS Physical Gold Token is a digital asset that represents ownership of one gram of physical gold. The actual gold is held in a secure vault managed by DBS Bank in Singapore, and the token provides a digital claim to it.

**2. Who can buy these tokenized gold products?**

The tokens will be available to DBS retail customers through the bank's digibank platform. The bank is also considering making them available to institutional and accredited investors via its DBS Digital Exchange (DDEx).

**3. Why is DBS tokenizing gold now?**

DBS has seen demand for physical gold from its wealth management clients more than double over the past three years. Tokenization allows the bank to meet this growing interest by offering a fractionalized, easily accessible, and secure product to a much broader retail audience.

**4. Is this different from a gold ETF?**

Yes, it is different. A token provides direct, fractional ownership of a specific amount of physical gold. While an ETF also tracks the price of gold, owning shares in an ETF represents a stake in a fund that holds gold, not a direct claim on the metal itself.

# Tokenized Gold: DBS Bank to Offer Retail Access Starting in 2026

Singapore’s largest bank, DBS, has announced it will provide retail clients access to **tokenized gold**, a move set to democratize ownership of the precious metal. The offering, scheduled for the second half of 2026, allows customers to buy DBS Physical Gold Tokens directly through the bank's popular digibank platform. This initiative follows a series of successful digital asset pilots, including the tokenization of structured notes on Ethereum and support for Franklin Templeton's money market fund token.

The introduction of a bank-grade tokenized commodity addresses a significant gap in the market. [According to the announcement](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/06/11/singapore-bank-dbs-to-offer-tokenized-gold-to-retail-customers), each token corresponds to one gram of physical gold, securely stored in a DBS vault in Singapore. This structure provides direct, fractional ownership of a real-world asset (RWA) with the security and trust of a major financial institution.

## DBS Paves the Way for Retail Gold Tokenization

The decision by DBS to bring a tokenized version of a traditional safe-haven asset to the retail market signals a major shift in digital finance. For years, direct access to physical gold has been predominantly reserved for institutional and high-net-worth investors. While retail customers could invest in gold-backed funds or ETFs, they did not have direct, divisible ownership of the underlying metal. This [new product changes that dynamic entirely](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/06/11/singapore-bank-dbs-to-offer-tokenized-gold-to-retail-customers).

The bank’s plan to manage the entire token lifecycle, from issuance to custody, ensures a closed-loop, secure environment. By avoiding third-party protocols or custodians, DBS minimizes counterparty risk and simplifies the user experience. Investors will be able to trade and hold the tokens within the familiar interface of their existing banking application.

### What is Tokenized Gold?

Tokenized gold represents physical gold recorded on a blockchain. Each digital token is a claim on a specific quantity of real gold held in a secure, audited vault. This digital wrapper allows the gold to be divided into smaller fractions, traded 24/7, and transferred almost instantly. It combines the intrinsic value of physical gold with the efficiency and transparency of blockchain technology.

## A Closer Look at Bank-Grade RWA Infrastructure

The integrity of any tokenized asset hinges on the quality of its underlying infrastructure. DBS is leveraging its status as a regulated financial institution to offer what it calls 'bank-grade' tokenization. This approach is designed to build confidence among both retail and institutional investors who may be wary of decentralized alternatives. The bank is also exploring a potential listing on the DBS Digital Exchange (DDEx), which would expand access to accredited investors.

### The Significance of In-House Custody

By managing custody internally, DBS provides a level of assurance that is often missing in the broader digital asset space. Each token is directly backed by physical bullion held in the bank’s own Singapore-based vault. This vertical integration means customers have a direct claim on gold held by a trusted, regulated entity, removing layers of complexity and potential points of failure. The bank has noted that demand for physical gold from its wealth clients has more than doubled in the last three years, highlighting the timeliness of this retail-focused product.

### Building on Previous Digital Asset Success

This venture is not DBS's first entry into the world of tokenization. The bank has been an active participant in Singapore's Project Guardian, an initiative exploring institutional DeFi. In 2025, DBS successfully tokenized structured notes on the Ethereum network and listed sgBENJI, the token for Franklin Templeton’s money market fund. This experience with different forms of RWAs has provided a strong foundation for launching a more ambitious retail product.

## Context and Future Outlook for Tokenized Assets

The move by DBS is part of a much larger trend toward the tokenization of real-world assets. From real estate and private equity to commodities and fine art, financial institutions are exploring ways to make traditionally illiquid assets more accessible and efficient. The market for RWAs is projected to expand into a multi-trillion dollar industry by 2030.

### The Broader Trend of RWA Tokenization

Financial analysts see RWA tokenization as a critical bridge between traditional finance (TradFi) and the emerging digital asset economy. By placing real assets on a blockchain, issuers can unlock new liquidity, automate complex processes like dividend payments, and reach a global investor base. DBS’s initiative with gold serves as a powerful blueprint for other banks, demonstrating how to merge the security of traditional finance with the innovation of blockchain. As regulatory frameworks mature, we can expect to see an acceleration of similar products from major financial players worldwide.

## Conclusion

DBS Bank's plan to offer **tokenized gold** to retail customers is a landmark development in the adoption of real-world assets. By providing a secure, regulated, and accessible way to invest in physical gold, the bank is setting a new standard for how traditional assets can be integrated into the digital economy. For traders and investors, this move opens up a new, highly liquid avenue for portfolio diversification, backed by the trust of a global financial leader.

## FAQs

**1. What is a DBS Physical Gold Token?**

A DBS Physical Gold Token is a digital asset that represents ownership of one gram of physical gold. The actual gold is held in a secure vault managed by DBS Bank in Singapore, and the token provides a digital claim to it.

**2. Who can buy these tokenized gold products?**

The tokens will be available to DBS retail customers through the bank's digibank platform. The bank is also considering making them available to institutional and accredited investors via its DBS Digital Exchange (DDEx).

**3. Why is DBS tokenizing gold now?**

DBS has seen demand for physical gold from its wealth management clients more than double over the past three years. Tokenization allows the bank to meet this growing interest by offering a fractionalized, easily accessible, and secure product to a much broader retail audience.

**4. Is this different from a gold ETF?**

Yes, it is different. A token provides direct, fractional ownership of a specific amount of physical gold. While an ETF also tracks the price of gold, owning shares in an ETF represents a stake in a fund that holds gold, not a direct claim on the metal itself.
